On a finite set of size n, an injective self-map has image size n and is surjective, so injectivity already implies the row identity. Distinct rows cannot share a1 in a column, and two columns with1 in one row would contradict injectivity of p and e. B is therefore0/1 with at most one1 in both rows and columns; missing1s record leakage. A chosen zero:Fin ancilla requires a nonempty ancilla carrier; a zero-qubit ancilla has dimension1. A zero-dimensional system gives an empty clean block, not an obligation to choose a system index.
